comparator.name: Molecular and Biophysical Life Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 programme comprises 75 EC of foundation courses, a 15 EC research project, 45 EC of major electives and 45 EC of free electives. The four profiles guide elective choices. The example shows the compulsory courses and the requirements for both elective blocks.
components: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Choose six approved courses, with at least 30 EC at advanced level.
Start after passing the foundation courses and earning at least 120 EC. The project can involve laboratory or computational research.
Choose eligible courses to deepen or broaden your studies.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biomolecules and the processes that make life possible
Chemistry, pharmaceutical science and molecular explanations of health, disease and medicines
Biological physics, mathematics and quantitative modelling of living systems
Experimental molecular biology, biochemistry, microscopy and laboratory research
Programming, statistics, bioinformatics and analysis of biological data
Genes, organisms, development, immunity and interactions across biological scales
adjacent: Genes to Organisms and Molecules & Cells
Molecules & Medicine, pharmacology, infection and drug innovation
Biophysics & Modeling, computational biology and quantitative life science
questions: How do molecular and cellular processes generate biological function and disease?
How can experiments, imaging and computation reveal the behaviour of cells and biomolecules?
How can molecular life science contribute to medicines and societal challenges?

alternatives.label: Molecular Life Science, Evolution and Biological Data
alternatives.labelReason: Study cells, genes, metabolism and disease through life science and laboratory work. Follow biological processes from molecules to organisms and populations through physiology, evolution and ecology. Use statistics, numerical modeling and imaging to analyze biological questions.
alternatives.concept: Study cells, genes, metabolism and disease through life science and laboratory work. Follow biological processes from molecules to organisms and populations through physiology, evolution and ecology. Use statistics, numerical modeling and imaging to analyze biological questions.
progression: The life science gateway precedes cell biology, anatomy, biochemistry and advanced disease work. Cell biology and biochemistry precede the laboratory. Programming and data literacy precede machine learning and imaging.

alternatives.label: Molecular Medicine and Human Health
alternatives.labelReason: Study the molecular basis of disease, infection and drug action alongside human physiology. Add epidemiology, health psychology and development to examine how disease and treatment affect people. Research methods help you evaluate health evidence.
alternatives.concept: Study the molecular basis of disease, infection and drug action alongside human physiology. Add epidemiology, health psychology and development to examine how disease and treatment affect people. Research methods help you evaluate health evidence.
progression: The gateways precede the biomedical and behavioral specialisms. Cell biology and biochemistry precede the laboratory; experimental methods precede evidence synthesis.
alternatives.distinctness: Study the molecular basis of disease, infection and drug action alongside human physiology. Add epidemiology, health psychology and development to examine how disease and treatment affect people. Research methods help you evaluate health evidence. Each plan has 6 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.

alternatives.label: Quantitative Life Science and Imaging
alternatives.concept: Combine cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work with linear algebra, numerical modeling, signals, machine learning and image processing. These methods support quantitative life science. Utrecht offers dedicated biological physics and structural biology that this plan cannot reproduce.
alternatives.labelReason: Combine cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work with linear algebra, numerical modeling, signals, machine learning and image processing. These methods support quantitative life science. Utrecht offers dedicated biological physics and structural biology that this plan cannot reproduce.
alternatives.distinctness: Combine cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work with linear algebra, numerical modeling, signals, machine learning and image processing. These methods support quantitative life science. Utrecht offers dedicated biological physics and structural biology that this plan cannot reproduce. Each plan has 4 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 7 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.
progression: Programming and data science precede computer vision and machine learning. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra and systems modeling. Cell biology and biochemistry precede the laboratory.

trace: Data cleaning, visualization and transformation support empirical inquiry.
Classification, prediction and model evaluation support analysis of biological data.
Segmentation, feature extraction and image classification provide methods transferable to biological imaging.
Neural network implementation supports quantitative pattern recognition in complex data.
Python programming and debugging provide computational foundations for modeling.
Calculus and mathematical methods provide foundations for quantitative life science.
Matrices and vector spaces provide tools for multivariate data and dynamic models.
Numerical differential equations and stability analysis provide tools for modeling biological systems.
Signals, transfer functions and state-space models support analysis of dynamic systems.
Probability distributions, estimation and simulation support quantitative inference.
Molecular and quantitative genetics, adaptation and evolutionary genomics connect genes to populations.
Population dynamics and organism–environment interactions extend the genes-to-organisms study into ecology.
Moral theories provide tools for reasoning about biomedical decisions and obligations.
Study design, confounding and risk measures support interpretation of population health evidence.
Functional anatomy and imaging connect body structure to physiological function.
Drug–receptor interactions, kinetics and toxicity support the study of medicines.
Innate and adaptive immunity and host–pathogen interactions develop mechanisms of infection.
Organ-system pathology and case reasoning connect physiology to disease.
Nervous system structure, evolution and regulation introduce biological bases of behavior.
Neural mechanisms of sensation and action connect biological function to behavior.
Attention, memory and neurophysiology extend the study of neural function.
Core biomolecules, metabolism and gene expression provide a life science foundation.
Neural signaling, anatomy and brain development support later neurobiology.
Cell organization, membranes, gene regulation and signaling directly support molecular cell biology.
Homeostasis and organ-system physiology connect cell function with organismal function.
Enzymes and metabolic pathways develop biochemical analysis of living systems.
Culture, protein purification, PCR and DNA analysis develop practical molecular methods.
Molecular pathology, genetic variation and gene-based therapies connect mechanisms with disease.
Experimental designs, regression and inference support empirical research.
Health behavior, stress and illness experiences complement the study of molecular disease.
Systematic reviews, bias appraisal and meta-analysis support evaluation of health evidence.
Developmental and health trajectories, genetics and environment support the medicine option’s lifespan context.
blocks: Both study cell organization, membranes and molecular processes.
Both examine biomolecules and the chemistry of living systems.
Both study how organisms function. UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Utrecht studies organic chemistry of drug molecules. UCR Pharmacology covers related drug action and disposition.
Both develop practical molecular and biochemical laboratory skills.
Both develop statistical reasoning. Utrecht also integrates academic writing in this course.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC research project. UCR independent research is optional and outside the scheduled degree.
Both develop mathematics for quantitative life science. UCR teaches programming in a separate course.
Utrecht provides dedicated physical chemistry and spectroscopy.
Utrecht applies physical principles directly to biological systems. UCR provides related mathematics and biology.
Utrecht teaches structural biology and biophysical laboratory methods as a dedicated course.
Utrecht includes 45 EC of free electives.
Utrecht requires six major electives. Its four advisory profiles help students choose their own combination.

selection.assessment: The broad option connects molecular and cellular life science to evolution, ecology and data. The medicine option emphasizes disease, drug action, health and development. The quantitative option has a coherent mathematics and imaging sequence distinct from the biological breadth of the closest option. The pairs differ by 1/2: 6 courses, 1/3: 4 courses, 2/3: 7 courses. Genes to Organisms and Molecules & Cells are addressed within the closest plan. Specialist biological physics, organic synthesis and structural-biology methods remain material gaps. Three options are retained.

notes.text: Both universities offer molecular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work and quantitative study. Utrecht requires dedicated physical chemistry, organic chemistry, biological physics and structural biology. Its 15 EC research project is compulsory. UCR offers optional independent research alongside its course-based plans.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s English-taught bachelor studies living systems through biology, chemistry, physics and pharmaceutical science.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 curriculum shows the required foundation and research project and leaves elective choices open. The three UCR plans emphasize molecular life science and evolution, medicine and health, or quantitative life science and imaging.
